we propose and analyze a novel distributed machine learning algorithm for fitting linear models with sparse data across heterogeneous nodes, and show that it outperforms the state-of-the-art methods in the literature.

, in a distributed setting where the sparsity of differences is smaller than the root sparsity, the proposed method is able to achieve a better performance in terms of both sample complexity and computational complexity, with respect to the group Lasso and the independent methods, and that the performance of the distributed methods is comparable with that of the centralized methods.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we show that it is advantageous to exploit the similarity structure between the data sets, and that this advantage can be quantified by our theoretical guarantees.
we provide finite sample guarantees that show that distributed methods can be more sample efficient than solving problems independently.

we propose a distributed method for sparse linear regression with heterogeneous data, and we show that it can achieve faster recovery rates compared to the standard group Lasso, and compared to the case where the problems are solved independently.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the sparsity of differences can be used to reduce the communication overhead in a distributed learning setting.
the graph structure of the data can be used as a guide for the design of distributed machine learning algorithms.
, by leveraging the sparsity of differences, we can reduce the sample complexity of the distributed setting.
